You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Prisma/Postgres, separate worker/ process). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/**; API under app/api/**; logic in lib/**; schema in prisma/schema.prisma.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do NOT touch the live database or live game infrastructure. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-05a-games-freemc.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. Purpose: 'nothing gets lost' capability safety net.

EFFICIENCY: batch independent shell calls; use grep/sed ranges over whole-file reads for large panel components.

CONTEXT FROM A COMPLETED SIBLING AUDIT (do not re-derive): paid game servers live in app/dashboard/games/** for the LIST, but a game server's detail page is /dashboard/servers/{id} — the same route as VPS, with a game-specific panel. Free Minecraft is app/dashboard/free-minecraft/** and is an orphan route with no sidebar entry.

YOUR AUDIT: GAME SERVERS (paid) + FREE MINECRAFT TIER capability inventory.
Produce:
1. Data models + status enums + lifecycle for both; how a game server row differs from a VPS row in the same table/model.
2. CAPABILITY TABLE for paid game servers: action | UI location (file + tab) | API route | backend fn | infra effect | danger level | state handling | reversible | notes. Cover every panel tab and every action, including: console/RCON commands, scheduled tasks, backups (create/restore/download/schedule), file manager (upload/edit/unzip), mods/plugins (what actually installs vs what is only a catalogue), player management (whitelist/ban/op/kick), world management (reset/upload/download/seed), server properties/settings editor (full field list + schema source file), version change/reinstall, startup params, subdomain/DNS, resource meters, activity/history, upgrade/downgrade plan, renew/cancel, delete, transfer, connect info.
3. Same CAPABILITY TABLE for free Minecraft (power/console/players/settings/presets/rename/change-domain, game modes, mod menu, inventory editor, LuckPerms roles/permissions, public server directory, auto-sleep/wake, subdomain routing, quotas/limits, upgrade-to-paid path). Note explicitly what is SHARED with the paid panel (the settings schema reuse) and what is duplicated.
4. The games catalogue: full table of games (name, slug, display name, category tags, image assets present, player counts, RAM, mod support flag, price-from) and the source file; note remaining slug/display-name inconsistencies and missing images.
5. Deployment wizard for games: exact steps and fields, which affect price/region/capacity (required pre-payment) vs changeable later (cite the API), the post-payment flow and the provisioning states the client can truthfully show (worker job chain + DB status fields + polling endpoint). State clearly which finer-grained steps the backend does NOT report.
6. Plans/pricing source, regions, promos affecting games.
7. Team/permission gating.
8. Gaps: backend capabilities not exposed in UI; UI stubs/no-ops.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary.

model GamePlan {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  gameFamily   String // minecraft, valheim, rust, palworld, cs2, terraria, ...

  basePlan     Plan     @relation(fields: [basePlanId], references: [id])
  osTemplateId String? // the game's OsTemplate (image) to deploy
  featured     Boolean  @default(false)
  active       Boolean  @default(true)
  sortOrder    Int      @default(0)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  servers      Server[]
}

/// Mod-manager CATALOG: an installable mod/plugin for a game family. One row per
/// mod per family; customers browse these and one-click install onto their server.
/// Seeded from the per-game mod deep-dive research (name/category/source/id).
model GameMod {
  id               String      @id @default(cuid())
  gameFamily       String // minecraft, rust, valheim, cs2, ark-ase, ark-asa, palworld, terraria, project-zomboid, ...
  name             String
  slug             String // stable per-family kebab identifier
  category         String // Admin, Protection, Economy, Performance, Content, QoL, ...
  // Where it comes from + how the installer fetches it. One of: modrinth, curseforge,
  // hangar, spigotmc, steam_workshop, thunderstore, umod, codefling, nexus, ficsit,
  // rocketmod, factorio_portal, mcpedl, github, manual.
  source           String
  sourceId         String? // workshop id / curseforge project id / modrinth slug / etc.
  url              String?
  modStringId      String? // e.g. Project Zomboid's Mods= string id (distinct from the numeric Workshop id)
  appliesToVariant String? // restrict to a loader/variant (e.g. "paper", "oxide", "carbon"); null = any
  description      String?
  iconUrl          String?
  popularity       Int         @default(0) // higher = more popular (sort key)
  paid             Boolean     @default(false)
  featured         Boolean     @default(false)
  active           Boolean     @default(true)
  createdAt        DateTime    @default(now())
  updatedAt        DateTime    @updatedAt
  installs         ServerMod[]

  @@unique([gameFamily, slug])
  @@index([gameFamily, category])
}

/// A mod/plugin installed (or being installed/removed) on a specific game server.
/// The worker's GAME_MOD_INSTALL / GAME_MOD_UNINSTALL handlers drive status.
model ServerMod {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  serverId    String

  error       String? // last failure detail, surfaced in the portal

  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  @@unique([serverId, modId])
  @@index([serverId])
}

/**
 * Real (not cosmetic) "what's actually happening right now" progress labels for
 * <ProvisioningOverlay/>, for both Shared Hosting and VPS/game-server orders.
 *
 * The provisioning workers (worker/hosting.ts, worker/index.ts) run in a SEPARATE
 * process from the web app (nxeon-worker.service vs nxeon-web.service), so an
 * in-memory signal (like lib/chat-bot-step.ts's TTL map, which works because the
 * chat bot and the poll route share one process) is not visible here — the signal
 * has to be durable. `HostingAccount.provisioningStep` / `Server.provisioningStep`
 * are those durable, best-effort columns: the worker writes a short human label
 * between real, observable command groups, and this module reads it back. A null
 * step means "no real signal yet" — callers fall back to generic/cosmetic text
 * rather than claiming false precision.
 *
 * For Shared Hosting specifically, "real progress" continues past the account
 * going ACTIVE: a one-click app install (WordPress, etc.) queued at order time
 * runs as a `HostingTask` AFTER the account is active, and that queue already has
 * genuine DB-persisted status transitions (PENDING → RUNNING → DONE/FAILED) — no
 * new instrumentation needed there, just a kind → label mapping.
 */

import { db } from "./db";

const HOSTING_TASK_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {
  WORDPRESS_INSTALL: "Installing WordPress…",
  APP_INSTALL: "Installing your application…",
  PHP_SWITCH: "Switching PHP version…",
  BACKUP: "Creating a backup…",
  RESTORE: "Restoring your backup…",
  CREATE_SUBDOMAIN: "Setting up your subdomain…",
  DELETE_SUBDOMAIN: "Removing your subdomain…",
  CREATE_ADDON_DOMAIN: "Connecting your domain…",
  DELETE_ADDON_DOMAIN: "Removing your domain…",
  CREATE_CRON: "Scheduling your cron job…",
  DELETE_CRON: "Removing your cron job…",
  INSTALL_DBTOOL: "Installing the database manager…",
  ENSURE_DBMGR: "Preparing your database manager…",
  APPLY_PLAN_LIMITS: "Applying your new plan…",
  RESET_DB_PASSWORD: "Resetting your database password…",
  SET_PRIMARY_DOMAIN: "Switching your primary domain…",
};

/**
 * The real step label for a Shared Hosting account, or null if there's nothing
 * genuine to say right now.
 *
 *  - PENDING/PROVISIONING: the account's own `provisioningStep` column, or a
 *    generic fallback if the worker hasn't written one yet (e.g. SANDBOX mode,
 *    which completes before any step is ever recorded).
 *  - ACTIVE: the label for whichever content task (WordPress/app install, PHP
 *    switch, …) is PENDING or RUNNING for this account, if any. This is what
 *    lets <ProvisioningOverlay/> keep showing progress through a post-order
 *    WordPress install even though the account itself is already ACTIVE.
 *  - Anything else (SUSPENDED/FAILED/DELETING, or ACTIVE with no live task):
 *    null.
 */
export async function hostingProvisioningStep(accountId: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const account = await db.hostingAccount.findUnique({
    where: { id: accountId },
    select: { status: true, provisioningStep: true },
  });
  if (!account) return null;
  if (account.status === "PENDING" || account.status === "PROVISIONING") {
    return account.provisioningStep || "Setting up your hosting account…";
  }
  if (account.status === "ACTIVE") {
    const task = await db.hostingTask.findFirst({
      where: { accountId, status: { in: ["PENDING", "RUNNING"] } },
      orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" },
      select: { kind: true },
    });
    if (task) return HOSTING_TASK_LABELS[task.kind] ?? "Finishing setup…";
  }
  return null;
}

  **and** the PayPal/Coinbase actions, so all payment rails parse one shape.
  A malformed `config` blob is dropped, not trusted.
- `gameOrderQuote(intent)` — resolves the `GamePlan` (allows the one-off custom
  tier via `CUSTOM_PLAN_SORT_ORDER` even though it is `active:false`), resolves
  the `OsTemplate`, validates hostname, validates variant + config
  (`validateConfig`, including `required` string fields like DST's Klei `TOKEN`),
  **requires and reserves a subdomain for `minecraft`**, then prices:
  `chargeCents = termPriceCents(monthlyCents, term, annualPct) + ipCents`.
- `placeGameOrder(user, intent, sold?)` — capacity check, `scheduleNode`, atomic
  wallet debit + `Server` create + `PROVISION` job + invoice. `sold` (card path)
  is the price stamped on the Checkout session **before** the card cleared, so
  fulfilment never re-prices.

Entry actions: `payAndDeployGame` (`lib/actions-gameplans.ts:201`),
`orderGameServer` (:285), and `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` for the card path.

### 5.3 Post-payment provisioning — what the client can truthfully show

Chain: `PROVISION` job → `worker/index.ts provision()`.

Durable signals the portal can read:

| Signal | Column / source | Written where |
|---|---|---|
| Coarse status | `Server.status`: `PENDING → PROVISIONING → RUNNING` (or `ERROR`) | `worker/index.ts:438`, `:746` |
| Terminal failure reason | `Server.provisionError` | ERROR path; cleared on retry (`retryProvision`) |
| **Live step label** | `Server.provisioningStep`, read by `serverProvisioningStep()` (`lib/provisioning-step.ts`) | `worker/index.ts` `step()` helper (:445) |
| Job history | `Job` rows (Activity tab) | |

The **complete set of real step labels** (`grep 'step("' worker/index.ts`) —
only **six**:

1. `"Allocating your server…"` (:546)
2. `"Configuring the network…"` (:576)
3. `"Starting your server…"` (:640)
4. `"Booting the operating system…"` (:652, skipped in SANDBOX)
5. `"Waiting for network access…"` (:677)
6. `"Starting the game server…"` (:695)

Then `status → RUNNING`, `provisioningStep → null`.

**Polling**: there is **no dedicated polling endpoint**. The page is
`dynamic = "force-dynamic"` and `components/AutoRefresh.tsx` triggers a full
route refresh every ~5 s while `transitional`;
`components/customer/ProvisioningOverlay.tsx` renders `liveStep` when present and
falls back to cosmetic time-based cycling text when it is `null`. Its own header
comment states it deliberately adds no new polling loop.

**Finer-grained steps the backend does NOT report** — a redesign must not invent
progress for any of these:

- No percentage / ETA of any kind (`Job.progress` is populated for
  `BACKUP_CREATE`/`BACKUP_RESTORE`, **not** for `PROVISION`).
- No sub-steps inside "Allocating" (disk clone %, image download, IPAM/OVH IP
  allocation, cloud-init snippet write).
- No signal for game-binary/SteamCMD download or first-world generation — the
  only game-specific checkpoint is the single `"Starting the game server…"`
  before the `GAME_PORT` probe (`worker/provision-health.ts`).
- No mod/plugin install progress at deploy time (mods are only installed later,
  via `GAME_MOD_SYNC`).
- No DNS/SRV propagation state for the chosen subdomain (`SYNC_GAME_DNS` is a
  separate job enqueued at `worker/index.ts:731/1034/1043/1287`; its state is
  only visible as a `Job` row).
- No "game service healthy" signal after provisioning — as noted in §1.1, the
  running-ness of the game process is never persisted.

## 6. Plans, pricing, regions, promos

| Topic | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Price source** | `GamePlan.priceCents` **only**, DB-fed. `monthlyCents = priceCents / max(1, termMonths)`; `chargeCents = termPriceCents(monthlyCents, term, annualPct) + ipCents` | `lib/game-order.ts:270-284` |
| **Displayed = charged = renewed** | Yes, by design. `lib/renewal-charge.ts:110-190` bills `gamePlan.priceCents` with **no** extra-disk or backup add-on lines ("a game plan is all-in") | |
| **Seed / catalogue** | `prisma/seed-gameplans.ts` (6 families, 14 tiers) + `seed-wave{1,2,3,4,7,8,9}-games.ts` + `seed-plutonium.ts`. `basePlanId` = the smallest active VPS `Plan` with `ramMB >= tier.ramMB` | |
| **Terms** | 1 or 12 months (`normalizeProductTerm`, `PRODUCT_TERMS`). Annual discount is a live admin setting (`annual_discount_percent`) **frozen onto `Server.annualDiscountPct` at sale** | `lib/annual-discount.ts`, `lib/billing-terms.ts` |
| **Custom tier** | "Build a custom server" creates a one-off `GamePlan` + backing `Plan`, both `active:false` with `sortOrder = CUSTOM_PLAN_SORT_ORDER` so no generic `where:{active:true}` query surfaces them | `lib/custom-plan.ts`, `lib/custom-plan-pricing.ts` |
| **Regions** | **None.** No region field on `Node`, `Plan`, `GamePlan` or `Server`. Node selection is automatic by RAM capacity (`scheduleNode`). Single region (SGP) | `prisma/schema.prisma` `model Node` |
| **Promos** | **Game never gets a promo.** `termPromoPercent` is stamped `0` for a flat game price. The first-month-free promo is **shared-hosting only** — `lib/game-order.ts:16-18` is explicit: *"no first-month-free on game … no $0 path, no coupon, no VAT change here"* | |

## 7. Team / permission gating

- **Ownership only.** Every game action funnels through `ownedServer()`
  (`lib/actions-game-control.ts:63`, `lib/actions-mods.ts:21`,
  `lib/actions-game-config.ts`), which allows `server.userId === user.id`
  **or** `user.role === "ADMIN"`. Same rule in `app/api/files/[serverId]/route.ts`
  and `app/api/servers/[id]/*`.
- **Free Minecraft is stricter**: every action is keyed on
  `db.freeMinecraftServer.findUnique({ where: { userId: user.id } })` — there is
  no admin-impersonation path in the customer actions at all (admin has separate
  tooling: `components/admin/FreeMinecraftControls.tsx`,
  `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`).
- **`Organization`/`Membership` exist in the schema** (roles `OWNER|ADMIN|MEMBER|BILLING`,
  plus a per-member `areas` JSON allowlist) and are used by
  `app/dashboard/team/**`, `lib/actions-teams.ts`, `lib/actions-gdpr.ts`,
  `lib/actions-hosting-db.ts` — but **not one game-server or free-Minecraft code
  path consults them**. A team member cannot be granted access to a teammate's
  game server; there is no per-server sharing, no delegated console/file access,
  no read-only role.
- Rate limits are the only other gate, all per-user per-minute
  (`throttle(user.id, op, max)`): power 20, logs 40, rcon 30, players 40,
  player-action 20, mc-mgmt 30, worlds 30, backups 30, backup-create 6,
  schedules 30, customDomain 10, customDomainVerify 6; free-MC: create 5,
  power 10, rcon 20, preset 10, subdomain 5 per 5 min.
- Additional per-action gates: `assertEmailVerified` (free-MC create only —
  paid game orders do **not** require a verified email), `lifecycleBusy`
  (9 exclusive `JobType`s), `gameJobInflight`, and `hasInflightJob` (mods/config
  refuse if **any** job is queued/running).

Summary (~10 lines):

1. **Models**: a paid game server is a plain `Server` row discriminated by `gamePlanId`; `planId` points at the *base* VPS plan that sizes the VM, never at what's billed. Game-only fields: `gameVariant`, `gameConfig`, `subdomain`, `autoUpdate`, `publicListing`, `customDomain`, plus `GameSchedule`/`ServerMod`/`PlayerSession`. Free Minecraft is a completely separate `FreeMinecraftServer` model (Docker container on `freemc-host`, no jobs, no billing, no worker).
2. **`ServerStatus` is the VM's status only** — whether the game process is actually up is never persisted anywhere.
3. **Biggest structural finding**: the game branch of `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` returns at line 1008, so the VPS `ServerTabs` never renders. That makes **Renew now, auto-renew, Cancel service, Delete, snapshots, networking, reinstall and VM-level power unreachable for every game customer**, and kills `GameManage.tsx` — which is the *only* consumer of the working `GAME_BACKUP` world-archive capability (`createGameBackup`/`getGameBackups`). The worker still emails "Download it from the Manage → Worlds tab", a tab that doesn't exist.
4. **RCON reality**: only `minecraft`, `cs2`, `palworld` have working RCON. Rust is declared-but-deferred; **44 of 47 families are `rcon:"none"`**, so console commands, player list, kick/ban, quick commands, roles and inventory are inert for them — and the panel only discovers this from an error-string regex.
5. **Two flag-gated features are effectively off in prod**: `GAME_CONFIG` saves (`ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG`) and mod installs (`ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS`). Both fail *honestly* rather than lying, but the customer copy promises a working feature. Even with the flags on, config appliers exist for 5 families and mod installers for 3 families / 4 of 15 sources. (Prod `.env` not read — marked UNVERIFIED.)
6. **Mod Store** fabricates ratings, install counts, screenshots, reviews and version history from `hash(slug)`; the version dropdown is display-only. Mods and Plugins are the same tab with a keyword filter.
7. **Worlds is read-only** (no reset/upload/download/seed; no `level-seed` field), the **file manager has no unzip**, and "Startup, environment & crash recovery" is an explicit *coming soon* stub.
8. **Wizard**: 4 steps (Game / Plan / Settings / Review). Game + tier + term + dedicated-IP are pre-payment and price-bearing; name, subdomain, variant and all config fields are changeable later. Tier changes are hard-refused post-sale by both `resize.ts` and `actions-server-lifecycle.ts` — and both error messages point at a settings control that doesn't exist. Provisioning reports exactly **6** coarse `provisioningStep` labels via a full-route 5s `AutoRefresh` (no polling endpoint, no %, no ETA, no per-phase game/mod/DNS progress).
9. **Free MC** reuses the paid `MINECRAFT` schema (`schemaFor("minecraft")` + `validateConfig`), the subdomain rules and the 26-node LuckPerms command catalogue; everything else (console, players, roles actions, inventory, settings UI) is duplicated. It has **no upgrade-to-paid path at all**, an unenforced disk quota, a send-only console, and both Mods and Roles gate on the *deprecated* `preset` column — which `applyFreeMinecraftSettings` sets to `"custom"`, silently disabling both tabs.
10. **Catalogue**: 47 families, 32 with config schemas, 30 with real art. `ark` points at the `ark-asa` art slug while the correct `ark-ase_*` files sit unused; `dayz_*` art is orphaned; 17 families ship with no hero/poster. No regions exist anywhere. Games never receive promos or coupons (schema supports `CouponServiceKind.GAME`, no code path reads it). Permissions are ownership-or-admin only — `Organization`/`Membership` exist but no game path consults them, so there is no per-server sharing or delegated access.
